InfoMat | ⭐ Review | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This review uniquely integrates mechanisms, advanced multiscale characterization (synchrotron methods, in situ sensors), and regulation of electrochemo-mechanical coupling across battery systems. Its novelty lies in framing mechanical effects as dual—beneficial for ion transport/kinetics and detrimental to structure—and in consolidating multiscale strategies from crystal and electrode to cell level, providing a unified framework for improving mechanical stability and long-term cycling performance.

item.title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a multi-modal operando platform combining pressure monitoring, EIS, and X-ray imaging to probe chemo-mechanical aging in solid-state Na||S cells. Its significance is revealing how electrolyte composition governs degradation: NPS causes localized sodium plating, while NPS-Cl improves interfacial stability and suppresses dendrites. This offers actionable guidance for sulfide electrolyte development and demonstrates operando diagnostics for resolving coupled chemo-mechanical phenomena.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an integrated Zr surface/subsurface strategy that converts residual Na₂CO₃/NaOH into a Na₂ZrO₃-rich nanolayer with near-surface Zr doping. This dual modification suppresses HF attack, transition-metal dissolution, cracking, and surface reconstruction, while reducing anisotropic lattice variation. Significantly, it raises capacity retention from 26.4% to 61.8% after 500 cycles, advancing O3-type sodium cathode stability.
